critical_issues.issue: Parsing of the task list may fail for formats not explicitly supported
critical_issues.why_it_matters: If the tool cannot correctly parse the file, it will produce no output or incorrect output, defeating its purpose of quickly identifying blocked tasks

critical_issues.issue: Assumes every blocked task has a responsible field
critical_issues.why_it_matters: Tasks without a designated responsible will cause the tool to either crash or omit critical information, leading to incomplete visibility for the user

fragile_assumptions: The task list file is stored locally and accessible
Each task contains a boolean field indicating if it is blocked
A field exists that identifies the person or dependency responsible for the block
The user has permission to read the task file
The list format is consistent and parseable
contradictions: Assumption that the format is consistent may conflict with real-world task lists that evolve or contain mixed entries
failure_modes: Parsing errors due to unexpected delimiters or encoding
Missing or malformed blocked/responsible fields causing runtime exceptions
Performance degradation on very large task files
missing_information: Exact file format (e.g., JSON, CSV, YAML) and schema of task entries
Encoding and line-ending conventions of the task file
How multiple blockers for a single task are represented
overclaims: Claim that the tool will be "small" despite potentially needing complex format detection and robust error handling
Implied guarantee of "quick" identification without accounting for large file sizes
